text:
jonathan: Heads up — hitting sustained GPU memory growth when KV paging is enabled on longer contexts (50k+ tokens). Noticed it on RTX6000 and H100, seems less severe on A100. repro + traces below.

sara: ugh. can you paste the minimal repro? is it deterministic for you? :thinking_face: 

jonathan: yes pretty deterministic. run loop below with paged_kv=true and page_size=64MB. after ~15 iterations resident goes up and page table has lots of holes.

jonathan: ```bash
# minimal repro (python env: py310, cuda 12.1)
python experiments/kv_repro.py --model gptj-6b --seq 51200 --paged_kv true --page_size 67108864 --iters 30
```

kevin: can you dump the page table stats from the runtime? slot counts / free lists?

jonathan: pasted below (trimmed):
```
PAGE_TABLE: total_pages=1024 used_pages=786 free_runs=238 fragmented_runs=63 avg_run_len=3.8
KV_POOL: total_slots=4096 used_slots=3072 reuse_hits=421 reuse_misses=2651
GPU_MEM: initial=12.4G cur=18.1G peak=19.3G
```

maria: those reuse_misses seem huge compared to reuse_hits — indicates our slot allocator isn't coalescing. could be ABA on the freelist?

kevin: also check whether small evictions create many tiny free runs (fragmentation). sounds like the page allocator is splitting then never merging because the buddy/merge logic depends on a timestamp that isn't updated on some GPUs. iirc we had a guard for compute capability >= 8.x that accidentally skipped on certain drivers.

jonathan: interesting — this repro runs on driver 535.54 on RTX and driver 525.x on H100. A100 uses 520.x. maybe a driver/atomics ordering difference.

infra-bot: deploys/1234 completed — runtime image pushed: gcr/redwood/runtime:kv-debug-2026-03-15

jonathan: i ran the image with extra debug flags and collected perf counters:
```
COUNTERS: kernel_kv_read_hits=1.2e6 kernel_kv_read_misses=4.8e5
kernel_merge_ops=0
memcpy_async_ops=420
```
Note kernel_merge_ops=0 which matches no coalescing.

sara: can you try toggling the atomic fallback to use the emulated CAS we added for older drivers? run with `--force_cas_emulation=true` and see if reuse improves.

jonathan: tried that — reuse_hits bumped to 1720 and reuse_misses dropped to 2400, GPU memory growth slowed but still present. Peak down ~600MB.

kevin: ok that strongly points at an atomic ordering bug in merge path. patch idea: add a versioned header per run and use CAS on header + small backoff before giving up merge. also add diagnostics to log failed merges with run addresses.

maria: agree. also add a periodic compaction pass that walks free runs and opportunistically merges neighbors every N iterations to mitigate long-running fragmentation for long-context workloads. make it optional and rate-limited.

jonathan: i've uploaded the full trace + heap map to s3://redwood-debug/kv/1789456123/trace.tar.gz and annotated the spots where merges were attempted but aborted.

sara: thanks. can you also include a short repro with the failing merge logging enabled? we should get exact allocator addresses and driver info so we can try to reproduce on internal A100/H100 lab.

jonathan: will do. adding a small patch to runtime to log `MERGE_FAIL addr=0x... reason=atomic_mismatch driver=535.54` and re-run.

kevin: once we have logs we can try reproducing with different CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES mappings and with/without peer-to-peer enabled — sometimes PCIe peer setup affects ordering.

maria: timeframe — can we get a PR with diagnostics + optional compaction by EOD? if not, a short mitigation flag to disable paging for >32k contexts would be OK for now.

jonathan: i'll open two PRs: diagnostics+compaction (opt-in) and an emergency flag `--kv_paging_max_context=32768`. PRs will reference the trace and include test harness.

sara: perfect. once PRs land let's run long-run CI on H100 and RTX to verify memory plateau. add a perf regression entry if we change default behavior.

kevin: also add a microbenchmark that stresses allocate/free patterns leading to fragmentation so we don't regress again.

jonathan: noted. i'll post PR links here when ready. thanks all :thumbsup:
